In accordance with Article 30 of the Personal Information Protection Act, MADI discloses the purposes, categories, and retention periods for the processing of personal information, and will post a notice on its website in the event of any changes. Article 1 (Items of Personal Information Processed) The Company collects the minimum amount of personal information necessary to provide its services. The items collected are as follows: Website product inquiries and consultations: Name, email address, country, phone number, job title, organization/company name, inquiry details; Recruitment website job applications and recruitment inquiries: Required: Name, Address, Phone Number, Mobile Phone Number, Email, Resume (Nationality, Status as a veteran or person with a disability, Educational Background, Grades, Work Experience, Military Service, Overseas Residence and Training Activities, Social Activities, Language and Other Certifications, Awards, Hobbies, Special Skills, Self-Introduction, etc.) Optional: Additional application documents (detailed work history, personal statement, portfolio, etc.) MADI Service Provision: (Required) Full name, email address, (Optional) Phone number, organization name, anonymized clinical data (limited to research purposes; separate consent required) Product Technical Support: Email, Organization Name Automatically collected during use of internet services: IP address, cookies, MAC address, service usage history, device information, visit history, location information (limited to service improvement purposes) Article 2 (Purpose of Personal Information Processing) The Company processes the collected personal information for the following purposes: Website Product Inquiries and Consultations: Collecting and responding to inquiries regarding the MADI platform (AI Digital Twin Clinical Trial Solution) Recruitment Website Job Applications and Recruitment Inquiries: Conducting and managing the recruitment process, providing recruitment information, handling recruitment inquiries, and registering candidates in the talent pool. Provision of MADI Services: Providing the AI Digital Twin Clinical Trial Platform service, utilizing the virtual patient solution, and supporting research. Product Technical Support: Providing technical support for MADI products. Automatically Collected Information: Service improvement, analysis of usage statistics, and strengthening of security. Personal information will not be used for purposes other than those for which it was collected; if a new purpose arises, separate consent will be obtained. Article 3 (Processing and Retention Period of Personal Information) In principle, personal information will be destroyed without delay once the purpose has been achieved. Specific Retention Periods: Product Inquiries and Consultations: Until the user withdraws consent; Job Applications and Recruitment Inquiries via the Recruitment Website: 2 years; MADI Service Provision: Until the service is terminated (clinical research data is retained for 1 year after the study ends); Product Technical Support and Product Training Support: Until the user withdraws consent; separate retention may be required in accordance with laws and regulations (Commercial Act, Electronic Commerce Act, etc.) (e.g., 5 years for contract-related matters, 3 years for consumer complaints). Even upon withdrawal of consent, we may retain the minimum amount of information necessary to comply with legal obligations. In principle, MADI does not use or provide personal information without the data subject’s consent. However, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, the criteria for determining whether to use or provide personal information without the data subject’s consent are as follows: Whether there is a relevance to the original purpose of collection; whether the additional use or provision of personal information is foreseeable in light of the circumstances under which the personal information was collected or established processing practices; whether it unduly infringes upon the data subject’s interests; and whether necessary measures to ensure security, such as pseudonymization or encryption, have been taken. Article 4 (Outsourcing of Personal Information Processing) The Company may outsource the processing of personal information to the following entities. When outsourcing, the Company complies with Article 26 of the Personal Information Protection Act (restrictions on processing, restrictions on re-outsourcing, supervision, etc.). Any changes to the details of the entrustment will be announced on the website. Entrusted Entities and Tasks: Centum Internet: Data storage and infrastructure management; Recruitment Management System: Operation and management of the recruitment website. Article 5 (Destruction of Personal Information) Madi destroys personal information without delay once the retention period has expired or the purpose of processing has been achieved. If the Company is required by other laws and regulations to continue retaining personal information even after the retention period agreed upon with the data subject has expired or the purpose of processing has been achieved, the Company will transfer such personal information to a separate database (DB) or store it in a different location. Destruction Procedure: Destruction shall occur upon approval by the person in charge when grounds for destruction arise. Destruction Method: Electronic files shall be destroyed using technology that renders them irrecoverable, and physical records shall be shredded or incinerated. If retention is required by law, the data shall be stored separately in a distinct database. Article 6 (Rights and Obligations of Data Subjects and Methods of Exercise) Data subjects may exercise their rights with respect to Madi at any time, including the right to access, correct, delete, suspend processing, or withdraw consent regarding personal information, as well as the right to object to automated decisions or request an explanation thereof (hereinafter referred to as “exercise of rights”). Requests for access, etc., regarding personal information of children under the age of 14 must be made directly by a legal representative; data subjects who are minors aged 14 or older may exercise their rights regarding their own personal information either personally or through a legal representative. You may exercise your rights by submitting a written request or via email to Madi, and Madi will take action without delay. Additionally, when Madi receives a request for access, correction, deletion, or suspension of processing in accordance with data subject rights, Madi will verify whether the person requesting access is the data subject themselves or a legitimate representative. If a data subject requests the correction or deletion of personal information due to errors or other issues, Madi will not use or provide such personal information until the correction or deletion is completed. The rights set forth in Paragraph 1 may be exercised through a representative, such as the data subject’s legal representative or an authorized agent. Data subjects must not infringe upon their own personal information or the privacy of others—including personal information currently being processed by Madi—in violation of the Personal Information Protection Act or other relevant laws and regulations. Requests to access personal information or suspend its processing may be restricted pursuant to Article 35(4) or Article 37(2) of the Personal Information Protection Act. If other laws or regulations explicitly designate such personal information as subject to collection, the information may not be deleted even if a request for deletion is made. If the data subject has given consent to automated decision-making, has been notified in advance through a contract or other means, or if there is a clear legal provision, a refusal of automated decision-making will not be accepted; only requests for an explanation and review are permitted. Furthermore, requests to object to or request an explanation of automated decisions may be rejected if there are legitimate grounds, such as a risk of unjustly infringing upon another person’s life, body, property, or other interests. Madi will verify whether the person exercising their rights is the data subject or a legitimate representative, process the request without delay, and notify the data subject of the reason for any refusal. Article 7 (Measures to Ensure the Security of Personal Information) In accordance with Article 29 of the Personal Information Protection Act, Madi shall take the following measures to ensure the security of personal information: Administrative Measures: Establishment of internal management plans; regular training Technical Measures: Management of access rights to personal information processing systems; installation of access control systems; encryption of personal information; installation of security software Physical Measures: Locking and access control of locations where personal information is stored or kept Article 8 (Data Protection Officer and Requests for Access) Madi has designated a Data Protection Officer as described below to oversee all matters related to the processing of personal information and to handle complaints from data subjects and provide remedies for damages arising from such processing. Name: Kim Eun-seok Title: Data Protection Officer Email: eskim@madidt.com Data subjects may contact the Data Protection Officer and the designated department regarding any inquiries, complaints, or requests for redress related to the protection of personal information that arise while using Madi’s services. Madi will respond to and address data subjects’ inquiries without delay. Data subjects may submit requests to access their personal information to the department listed above in accordance with Article 35 of the Personal Information Protection Act. Madi will make every effort to ensure that data subjects’ requests to access their personal information are processed promptly. Article 9 (Remedies for Infringement of Rights) If a user needs to report or seek consultation regarding a personal information infringement, they may contact not only Madi’s Personal Information Protection Department but also the following agencies: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee (www.kopico.go.kr/ (dial 1833-6972 without an area code)) Personal Information Infringement Reporting Center (privacy.kisa.or.kr/(toll-free) 118) Cybercrime Investigation Division, Supreme Prosecutors’ Office (www.spo.go.kr/ (toll-free) 1301) Cyber Safety Bureau, National Police Agency (cyberbureau.police.go.kr/ (toll-free) 182) Article 10 (Amendments to the Privacy Policy) The Privacy Policy may be amended in response to the enactment or revision of laws, changes in government policy, changes in the Company’s internal policies, or changes in security technology; in such cases, we will announce the details of the changes on our website 7 days prior to the effective date. Hello, I am Kim Seong-hwan, CEO of MADI. As an orthopedic surgeon who has treated countless patients, I have witnessed the fundamental dilemmas inherent in clinical trials. These include the reality that some patients are assigned to the control group to validate new treatments and thus miss out on treatment opportunities, as well as the delays in new drug development caused by enormous costs and time constraints. MADI aims to solve these problems using AI technology. By creating “Digital Twins” through generative AI to generate virtual control groups, we are realizing ethical clinical trials where every patient can receive treatment. We are also striving to drastically reduce the duration and cost of clinical trials so that innovative treatments can reach more patients faster. The convergence of real-world medical experience and cutting-edge AI technology is MADI’s unique competitive advantage. We do not merely develop technology; we create solutions that deeply understand and address the needs of the actual healthcare setting. We are seeking passionate talent to join MADI in transforming the paradigm of clinical trials and shaping the future of medical AI. Your skills and passion can become a source of hope for countless patients. Thank you.
